title: Escape from Duckov (逃离鸭科夫)
genre: single-player PvE extraction looter-shooter (top-down) with base building; Escape from Tarkov parody
release_date: 2025-10-16 (PC: Steam, Epic Games Store; Windows + macOS)
developer: Team Soda (碳酸小队), an internal studio of bilibili; producer Jeff Chen
team_size: 5 people (4 before the demo launched) [CONFIRMED – producer Jeff Chen via Inven Global and ifeng interview; Game Developer reported 4]. Roles: producer (design + combat programming), designer (weapon/enemy numbers), lead designer (most programming), one 3D artist/level designer who built all maps and art assets, plus one more.
developer_background: Small team inside bilibili; previous games Soda Crisis (碳酸危机) and Snake Force (蛇行武装). Duckov sold in days what Soda Crisis took three years to reach. Producer Jeff Chen worked at bilibili for 7 years and has 1,400+ hours in Escape from Tarkov. The duck look came from an artist sketch during early art-style experiments.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3167020/Escape_From_Duckov/ ; Steam demo: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3464460/Escape_From_Duckov_Demo/ ; Epic Games Store (from May 2025 announcement); macOS. Console and mobile ports 'initiated' per bilibili chairman Chen Rui (Nov 2025), unreleased as of research date.
business_model: premium $17.99 / €17.99 / ¥58 in China (launch discount; later sales -12% to -30%); free updates, mod support (Steam Workshop) added after 1M sales; Escape from Tarkov crossover (2026-02-10)
units_or_downloads: 200k in 24h, 300k in 3 days, 500k by 2025-10-19 [CONFIRMED – bilibili/Team Soda via TechNode/PC Gamer]; 1,000,000 by 2025-10-22 (excluding refunds) [CONFIRMED – bilibili via GameSpot/Gematsu]; 2,000,000 by 2025-10-28 [CONFIRMED – Team Soda/bilibili via Game Developer/Inven Global]; 3,000,000+ by ~2025-11-08 [CONFIRMED – Team Soda milestone per Wikipedia; restated by bilibili chairman Chen Rui on the Q3 earnings call 2025-11-13 via Yicai]. Later: 3.3M+ copies, ~65% (2M) in China [ESTIMATE – Alinea Analytics, ~Dec 2025]; 3.8M Steam copies [ESTIMATE – Raijin, Aug 2026]. No official update after 3M found.
peak_concurrent_players: 301,322 on Steam, 2025-10-26/27 [CONFIRMED – SteamDB data via GosuGamers/GamesRadar; SteamCharts and Tracker.gg list 301,322; Raijin 301,244]. Earlier 221,963 on 2025-10-21. Monthly peak ~8.7k in the latest 30 days (~autumn 2026) [SteamCharts].
steam_reviews: 103,739 reviews, 84% positive all languages [Raijin, Aug 2026]; English-only 10,678 at 93% 'Very Positive' [Steam store page snapshot, undated]. The large gap shows the audience is mostly Chinese-speaking.
implied_review_multiplier: ~29–37 [ESTIMATE – 3.0M confirmed units ÷ 103.7k reviews (lower bound because reviews are dated later than units) up to 3.8M Raijin units ÷ 103.7k]. Lower than the 50–60 default for Chinese-audience games.
gross_revenue: ≈ $42–49M Steam gross by Aug 2026 [ESTIMATE – 3.8M units × $11–13 avg realised price; blended list price ≈ $11.6 given ~65% of copies at ¥58 (~$8) and 35% at $17.99, so 0.75 × US list ($13.49) would overstate it]. Trackers: $43M+ at 3.3M copies [ESTIMATE – Alinea]; $41.3M (Aug 2026; was $46.6M in Apr 2026 before model revision) [ESTIMATE – Raijin]. Chinese press: 'five people earned over ¥100M (~$14M) in two weeks' [ifeng headline]. Unsourced lead of $53M not confirmed.
net_revenue: ≈ $28–34M [ESTIMATE – $41–49M gross; Steam tiered cut (30% first $10M, 25% $10–50M) leaves $30.5–36.2M × 0.93]. Mid-case $45M gross → ~$31M net. All to bilibili (internal studio; any team bonus undisclosed). Epic sales not separately known.
production_cost: ≈ $0.2–0.4M direct dev cost [ESTIMATE – 4–5 people × ~18–24 months (assumed; see development_time) × $3k/month (China rate) ≈ $216k–360k], plus undisclosed bilibili marketing/PR (Gamescom 2025 presence, Next Fest, influencer promotion). No disclosed figure; Chinese press describes it as a 'small-cost' (小成本) game.
development_time: no confirmed figure. Timeline: Steam page and demo existed by Feb 2025 (demo trended on Steam's Trending Free), new demo 2025-05-29, Steam Next Fest June 2025, Gamescom Aug 2025, release 2025-10-16. Inferred ≥1–2 years [ESTIMATE].
why_popular: Takes the hardcore extraction-shooter loop (raid → loot → extract → upgrade base) from Escape from Tarkov and makes it single-player PvE: no cheaters, no PvP stress, pause-friendly, much easier to learn. Cute, meme-able ducks contrast with deep systems (weapons, attachments, crafting, hideout, quests). Cheap (especially ¥58 in China) and gentle on hardware. Huge Chinese domestic audience via bilibili's platform plus Western streamers who liked the parody. Called 'a full-fledged, full-featured singleplayer bottling of extraction shooter juice' (PC Gamer).
marketing_channels: Long demo-led funnel: early Steam demo (Feb 2025, trending), refreshed demo + Epic/Mac announcement (May 2025), Steam Next Fest (June 2025), Gamescom 2025 demos/interviews; bilibili's own video platform and Chinese streamers/UGC; Western YouTube/Twitch coverage after launch; Steam top-seller charts (beat Battlefield 6 and ARC Raiders on weekend CCU); post-launch mod support; Escape from Tarkov official crossover (Feb 2026) for renewed press.
engine: Unity [reported – Wikipedia; not stated by the developer in the sources found]
art_style: stylised, chunky low-poly 3D with cartoon ducks, top-down/isometric camera, clean readable UI
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write most of the systems code (top-down twin-stick shooting, enemy AI states, grid inventory, loot tables, raid/extract loop, base upgrades, quests, save system), generate low-poly props/weapons/characters (Meshy/Tripo with cleanup), icons for hundreds of items, item descriptions, SFX and music. Single-player, so no netcode. | AI cannot: balance an item economy and progression across hundreds of items, design maps that create tense extraction decisions, tune shooting feel and enemy difficulty, keep a consistent art style across many 3D assets, or replicate bilibili's distribution in China. Many interlocking systems make this a 3 rather than a 4. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 or Godot 4 + Steamworks/GodotSteam; Meshy/Tripo + Blender for low-poly 3D; Scenario/Midjourney for icons/UI; ElevenLabs SFX; Suno music; spreadsheet/JSON-driven item database generated and balanced with Claude-written simulation scripts.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 6–10 weeks, $300–$800 (1 map, 3 enemy types, 30–50 items, grid inventory, raid/extract loop, simple hideout; Claude Pro/Max, 3D gen, image/audio subs, Steam Direct $100)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 6–12 months, $4,000–$15,000 (4–5 maps, 200+ items, quests, base building, mod support; freelance 3D/animation polish $2–6k, localisation incl. Simplified Chinese $1–3k, demo + Next Fest + streamer outreach; excludes developer's own living costs)

data_conflicts: Team size 4 (Game Developer, pre-demo) vs 5 (Inven/ifeng/Niko, later) – used 5. Date of 3M: 2025-11-08 (Team Soda per Wikipedia) vs announced on bilibili's 2025-11-13 earnings call – both cited. Revenue: Alinea $43M+ (3.3M copies) vs Raijin $41.3M (Aug 2026, revised down from $46.6M) – used a $42–49M range; the $53M lead could not be sourced. Realised price is well below 0.75 × US list because ~65% of buyers are in China at ¥58. Engine Unity comes only from Wikipedia, not a dev statement. Dev time not found in 5+ searches (EN + CN).
notes: A strong template for a solo dev: take a beloved but punishing multiplayer genre (extraction shooters) and make an accessible single-player PvE version with a funny, memorable theme. A tiny team (one 3D artist built all maps and assets) shows scope can be controlled with low-poly art. A long public demo cycle (Feb → May → June Next Fest → Gamescom) built wishlists. Localising into Simplified Chinese and pricing for China mattered a lot: ~65% of sales were Chinese.
